Ready for the maintainer to merge at the next cut. No blocking findings.

The example conditions, guide heights and automatic threading meet issue #3214. Each condition and the machine description identify the examples. The guide gives replacement steps. The tests check posting, replacement of a condition, and taper refusals.

I reviewed this as a safety-tier change because the machine data changes posted output. I checked the six changed files against AGENTS.md at upstream/main 4d6b75e77. No golden files changed. No UI code changed, so screenshots are not required.

Results, run locally in an isolated worktree after a clean trial merge with upstream/main:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed. Both selected builds passed.
- Post `machine_tree`: 13 passed.
- Post `ream_lathe`: 7 passed.
- App `probe_no_coolant`: 5 passed.
- App `sodick_alc400g`: 6 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

Extra suites run:

- App `machine`: 33 passed.
- App `machine_library`: 16 passed.
- App `posting`: 17 passed.
- No fixture or importer changes require the additional kernel suites.

Heavy lane check: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selected `probe_no_coolant`. That source has no ignored tests. The changed Sodick suite also has no ignored tests. There are no applicable heavy tests. I did not count the dry run as a test pass.

Mutation checks, run locally:

1. Restore the old machine file: RED, with the three failures reported in the PR body.
2. Set `edm.awt` to false: RED. The first-contour test fails because T91 and T90 are absent.
3. Remove EXAMPLE from the condition notes: RED. The example-marker test fails on C110.
4. Restore the PR machine file: GREEN, all six Sodick tests pass. The worktree has no remaining changes.

Requested before merge: none.

Limits: no physical Sodick control was tested. The example values require replacement before cutting. The existing post warns that its control words are unverified and that each condition must exist in the control table. It still refuses tapered output.

The first gate attempt selected unrelated upstream changes before the trial merge was committed locally. I stopped it and ran the corrected quick gate above. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6f2c3cc87e7fa437ff6258504e745699b7acc114 -->
Second safety read (Opus, read-only): blockers

Scope: the head `6f2c3cc87` (one commit on top of `main`, no commit of another open PR). The PR is open and not merged. I read the diff, `assets/machines/sodick-alc400g.mch`, `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`, `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` and `crates/app/src/machine/wire_edm.rs` at the head. I did not build.

## Blocker

1. **The posted program does not say that its kerf comes from an example gap.**
   - The Wire Contour path is a wire-centre path. The offset is the wire radius plus the condition `gap` (`wire_op.rs`, `condition_of`). The Sodick post writes no G41 / G42 (`sodick-wire.cps:221`, `:272`).
   - With this PR, a user who does not edit the file gets a path with an offset of 0.125 + 0.04 = 0.165 mm. The 0.04 mm gap is an invented value.
   - The posted word `C110` then selects the real row C110 of the control's own table. That row can have a different gap, or it can be for a different wire or height. The part is then the wrong size by the gap difference. Wire EDM tolerances are in microns, so this is a wrong part.
   - Only the condition id goes to the post (`posting_wire.rs:230`, `PARAM EdmCondition`). The name "Rough cut (example)" and the `EXAMPLE` notes never get to the program. The program says only `CONDITION C110 MUST EXIST IN THE CONTROL CONDITION TABLE - CHECK ITS VALUES` (`sodick-wire.cps:318`). The operator cannot compare the control row with the gap that CamCraft used, because the program does not state that gap.
   - Before this PR, the same case was a visible refusal. After this PR, it is a silent post on invented data. This is against the Prime Directive ("correct, or visibly refused with a diagnostic").
   - Recommended fix (small): when a posted condition's `notes` start with `EXAMPLE`, write a program note and a post warning. For example: `CONDITION C110 IS AN EXAMPLE ROW - THE KERF USES AN EXAMPLE GAP OF 0.040 MM - REPLACE IT BEFORE CUTTING`. Also write the gap of each condition in its note, so the operator can compare it with the control row. Pin the note in `a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file`, and pin its absence in `a_punch_posts_through_the_sodick_post_on_it` (user row `C210`).

## Checked, no finding

- Clean room: the values are original, each is marked "EXAMPLE - not a Sodick figure", and the description says the same. No HSMWorks text, post or library is used. No third-party data, so no licence note is necessary.
- Guide heights 0 / 130 mm: they cannot reach posted U / V. The Sodick post refuses every taper (pinned). `wire-iso.cps` refuses this file because it states no `edm.codes` (`wire-iso.cps:143`). The guide-span check (`wire_verify.rs:54-67`) can now refuse work below Z0 or above Z130, but that is a refusal, not a wrong output.
- `awt: true`: on a machine without a threader, T91 / T90 give a control alarm, not a wrong cut. The guide says to set it to `false`. Note: `lower_guide_z` 0 and `awt` have no public source named; the decision file justifies only the 130 mm upper guide.
- Gaps 0.04 / 0.02 / 0.01 mm are smaller than the 0.125 mm wire radius and decrease from rough to finish. They are plausible as examples.
- No other machine, post or golden changes. Only `sodick_alc400g.rs` names this file in tests; `machine.rs:770` reads only its kind.
- The shipped file is loaded and posted in three tests. No new code on a user path; `expect` is in tests only. `sodick_alc400g.rs` has 204 lines.

Coordinator, for @mkinney: the second safety read on head 6f2c3cc87 (comment 7075321111) found one wrong-output blocker.

- The Wire Contour offset is the wire radius plus the condition `gap`. On the shipped Sodick ALC400 file, that gap is an example value (0.04 mm), not a Sodick figure.
- The posted program names only the condition id (`C110`). It does not state the gap that the offset used, and it does not say that the row is an example. If the real control's C110 has a different gap, the part has the wrong size, with no diagnostic.
- Before this PR, the same case was refused. Now it posts on invented data.
- A small fix is enough: when the notes of a condition start with `EXAMPLE`, write a program note and a post warning that give the example gap. Pin this in the shipped-file test.

I added `needs-rework` beside your `merge-ready`. I removed no label. The two collaborators decide on this PR. Please do not merge until the blocker is fixed or the disagreement is settled.

The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

This PR had both labels. The second safety read of the current head `6f2c3cc87` (NeoTech, 06:25:48Z) found blockers, and it stands. I removed `merge-ready`. The label `needs-rework` stays. The label `merge-ready` can return when a new head gets a clean review.

Addressed: the blocker of the second safety read on `6f2c3cc87` (the posted program does not say that its kerf comes from an example gap).

New head: `0c58a20324a400dd34a966a07fd86919183143ec`. The PR is a draft again because of this push.

## What changed

- The Sodick post now writes a note after each posted condition, for the cut and for each skim. The note gives the gap that the kerf offset used:
  `(CONDITION C210 KERF GAP 0.040 MM - COMPARE WITH THE CONTROL ROW)`
- If the `notes` of the row start with `EXAMPLE`, the note is a warning:
  `(WARNING CONDITION C110 IS AN EXAMPLE ROW - THE KERF USES AN EXAMPLE GAP OF 0.040 MM - REPLACE IT BEFORE CUTTING)`
- The post reads the gap from `machine.edm.conditions`. Before, the wire machine mirror did not send the table. Now `post::machine::mirror` sends `edm.conditions` for a wire machine when the file has a table. A wire file without a table mirrors as before.
- I did not add a post `message()` warning. In `posting::post_script`, any post message blocks the post ("post blocked - N warning(s)"). That would refuse the first Wire Contour that #3214 asks for. The program note is the diagnostic that the operator sees at the control. The decision file records this choice.

## Pins

- `sodick_alc400g::a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file`: asserts the WARNING line for C110 with the gap of 0.040 MM.
- `sodick_alc400g::a_punch_posts_through_the_sodick_post_on_it`: asserts the plain gap note for the user row C210, and that the program has no `EXAMPLE` text.
- Mutation check: with `conditionNotes()` disabled, the two tests fail (RED). Without the mirror change, the same two tests fail (RED). With the fix restored, the tests pass (GREEN).

## Goldens moved

The new note lines go into the four Sodick wire goldens. I regenerated them with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. No motion line changed.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_flushed.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_passes.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_passes_flushed.nc`

In `sodick_wire_passes`, the structural assertion now expects the gap note between the `SKIM` note and the C word.

## Gates on the new head

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 73 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 199 steps (app heavy, every target), 0 failed, 50.3 min.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 33 passed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

I did not test on a physical Sodick control.

Please do a re-review of the new head.

Ready for the maintainer to merge at the next cut. No blocking findings.

This is a safety-tier review. I checked the PR against AGENTS.md from upstream/main `16dc39f069ded367d46404157fd3652d37cd23f6`.

The new head resolves NeoTech's finding on `6f2c3cc87`. The posted program now states each cut and skim condition's gap. An EXAMPLE row gets a WARNING note that states the example gap and says to replace it before cutting. The machine mirror supplies the condition table. The tests check the example warning and its absence for the replacement row C210. The decision file explains why a program note replaces a blocking `message()` warning.

The starter conditions, guide heights, threader flag and replacement instructions meet issue #3214. The taper refusals remain tested. No UI code changed, so before/after screenshots are not required. The PR adds no dependency or build script.

Local results

All checks ran in `.claude/worktrees/review-3228` after a clean trial merge. The trial commit is `f71e5af2de4f32c1f41b420291ba459e9ce63fc1`. Its first parent is the PR head. Its second parent is the upstream/main SHA above. No GitHub runner was used.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 742 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 71.6 minutes. The changed goldens select the broad app suites.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 11.7 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 212 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 41.5 minutes.
- `cargo clippy -j 32 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- App `sodick_alc400g`: 6 passed; `sodick_wire_dielectric`: 3 passed; `sodick_wire_passes`: 5 passed; `sodick_wire_post`: 8 passed.

Heavy lanes green on 0c58a20324a400dd34a966a07fd86919183143ec: 212 steps, 0 failed. Base: upstream/main `16dc39f069ded367d46404157fd3652d37cd23f6`. Local record: `gate-logs/heavy-20261123-001414`.

Extra suites run

These suites ran by name in the quick gate:

- `example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored. `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed each.
- The three Sodick golden readers: `sodick_wire_post`, `sodick_wire_dielectric`, and `sodick_wire_passes`, with counts above.
- `conformance`: 7 passed; `solid_law_goldens`: 7 passed.
- `machine`: 33 passed; `machine_library`: 16 passed; `posting`: 17 passed.

The PR changes no importer or STEP fixture, so the extra kernel STEP suites do not apply.

Goldens moved

I checked all four listed `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/*.nc` diffs line by line. They add gap notes only: one line in each single-pass program, three in each multiple-pass program. No motion or control word changed. The PR body lists these files under Goldens moved.

Mutation checks

1. Disable `conditionNotes()`: RED. The shipped-file and replacement-row posting tests fail; the other four tests pass.
2. Remove the wire mirror's condition table: RED. The same two posting tests fail; the other four tests pass.
3. Restore both files: GREEN. All six starter-machine tests pass. The worktree has no tracked changes.

Requested before merge: none.

Limits: no physical Sodick control was tested. The example data requires replacement before cutting. The post still identifies its control words as unverified.

The review worktree and branch remain in place to keep the build warm. No evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Second safety read of head `0c58a2032` (read-only Opus agent, nothing built). This comment is not the review. The review of mkinney on this head stands.

**Result: no blocker.** The blocker of the first safety read on `6f2c3cc87` is fixed: an example gap now posts with a warning line.

- **Starter set.** `sodick-alc400g.mch` adds `C110` (rough, gap 0.04), `C120` (skim, gap 0.02) and `C130` (finish, gap 0.01) for a 0.25 mm wire. It adds `lower_guide_z` 0, `upper_guide_z` 130 and `awt: true`. No value has a public source. The description, each `notes` field and the decision file say so. No vendor material is copied.
- **Posted program.** `sodick-wire.cps` writes `(WARNING CONDITION C110 IS AN EXAMPLE ROW - ... - REPLACE IT BEFORE CUTTING)` at the cut start and at each skim. The pin is `a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file`.
- **The `.cps` change.** It adds `conditionRow` and `conditionNotes` and two calls. The four goldens change only by new `(CONDITION ... KERF GAP ...)` comment lines. No X/Y/U/V word, no `T91`/`T90`, no `T85`, no block order changes.
- **Old files.** A wire file with no table mirrors as before. `edm.conditions` is an existing field, so no project version step is necessary.
- **Example suites.** No example or catalog case uses this machine or this post.

Notes, none is a blocker:

1. The example warning is a program comment only. The app shows no warning, because a post `message()` blocks the post.
2. The example guide heights and `awt: true` have no EXAMPLE marker in the mirror or in the program. Today no post uses the guide heights: the Sodick post refuses each taper, and `wire-iso` refuses this file.

I file the two notes as `P7` follow-ups. The trial merge on the current main is in the queue. The merge follows a green trial.

Merge note. Class: no refresh (the reviewed head `0c58a2032` merged unchanged).

Basis:
- The review of mkinney on this head, and the second safety read above (no blocker).
- A trial merge on main `edcbfe4dd` (merge `1d5c00ef1`, not pushed): the `camcraft-post` crate 1036 passed, 0 failed; 17 named app binaries green, with `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `posting`, the Sodick binaries, the three `example_catalog` suites and `first_part_programs`; clippy on `camcraft-post --all-targets` and `camcraft-app --lib` is clean.
- Main moved to `5ce2abe61` after the trial started. The difference is one example file (`examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`, #3523). This PR and its tests do not use that file.

No heavy lane ran (`P4`, the heavy lanes run at the cut). The follow-ups are #3596 and #3597.
